input: Switch to a SIM card for Europe travel

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they need data only, calls and texts too, or a full replacement SIM determines which products are even eligible.
The specific countries visited and trip duration directly affect which plan offers the best coverage and value.
Whether this is for one person or multiple travellers changes whether a single SIM, a group plan, or a portable hotspot is more appropriate.
Budget per month or per trip sets a hard ceiling on which SIM or eSIM options are realistic.
Whether their phone is unlocked and eSIM-capable determines whether they can use a virtual eSIM or must buy a physical SIM on arrival.
Whether they want to keep their existing number active (via call forwarding or dual-SIM) or are happy to use a new number changes the setup entirely.
What 'working well' means to them — e.g. fast data for navigation, reliable calls home, or just basic connectivity — determines which plan metrics to prioritise.

gold.taskTitle: Switch to a SIM card for Europe travel
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to set up a SIM card solution for using their phone while travelling in Europe.

questions.title: Which services do you need — data, calls, texts?
questions.description: Establish whether the user needs a data-only plan, or also requires voice calls and SMS while abroad.

questions.title: Which countries and how many weeks are you travelling?
questions.description: Identify the specific European countries and the total trip duration to match coverage zones and plan lengths.

questions.title: Is this SIM just for you or for others too?
questions.description: Determine if the solution needs to cover a single traveller or multiple people, which could favour a hotspot or group plan.

questions.title: What is your total budget for connectivity on this trip?
questions.description: Capture the user's spending limit so only realistic SIM or eSIM options are considered.

questions.title: Is your phone unlocked and does it support eSIM?
questions.description: Find out the phone's compatibility to determine whether a physical SIM purchase or an eSIM activation is the right path.

questions.title: Do you need to keep your current number reachable?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user must receive calls and texts on their existing number, which affects whether a dual-SIM or call-forwarding setup is needed.

questions.title: What matters most — fast data, low cost, or reliable calls?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority so the plan recommendation is weighted towards the right performance metric.
